title: Quality Within a Project Life Cycle
subject: Project quality management
description: Thirty questions across easy, medium and hard on how quality is managed in each of the five phases of a project, from initiation to closure.

questions.prompt: What does quality within a project life cycle refer to?
options: Inspecting the project deliverables only at the point of handover
The systematic process of ensuring that activities, processes, deliverables and outcomes meet quality standards and stakeholder expectations from initiation to closure
The cost of correcting defects found after the project has closed
The set of standards the client chooses before the project begins
questions.explanation: The notes stress that quality runs through the whole project, from initiation to closure, and is not a last-minute check.

questions.prompt: How many major phases does a typical project life cycle have in these notes?
options: Five
Three
Four
Seven
questions.explanation: The five phases are initiation, planning, execution, monitoring and controlling, and closure.

questions.prompt: Which option lists the five phases of the project life cycle correctly?
options: Initiation, design, execution, handover, closure
Planning, procurement, execution, inspection, closure
Initiation, planning, execution, monitoring and controlling, closure
Initiation, planning, execution, testing, maintenance
questions.explanation: Each phase has its own quality activities that contribute to overall project success.

questions.prompt: Is project quality management something done only at the end of a project?
options: Yes, it is mainly a final inspection activity
Yes, because the earlier phases have no quality requirements
No, it belongs only to the planning phase
No, it must be integrated into every phase of the project life cycle
questions.explanation: The notes say quality management is not an activity performed only at the end of a project.

questions.prompt: How do the notes define project quality?
options: The number of defects found per deliverable
The extent to which the project is finished within budget
The degree to which a project's characteristics and deliverables fulfil specified requirements and stakeholder expectations
The amount of testing done on the final product
questions.explanation: Quality is about meeting specified requirements and stakeholder expectations, not just counting defects or staying on budget.

questions.prompt: Which phase involves identifying the project need, objectives, scope and stakeholders?
options: Project initiation
Project planning
Project execution
Project closure
questions.explanation: Initiation is the beginning of the project, where the need, objectives, scope and stakeholders are identified.

questions.prompt: Which activity belongs to the planning phase?
options: Obtaining client approval of the final deliverable
Identifying customer quality expectations
Conducting laboratory tests on completed work
Developing a project quality management plan
questions.explanation: Planning develops the quality plan, indicators, assurance procedures and control methods. The other options belong to closure, initiation and monitoring and controlling.

questions.prompt: Which phase includes final quality inspections and obtaining client approval?
options: Monitoring and controlling
Project closure
Project execution
Project initiation
questions.explanation: Closure formally completes the project, verifies deliverables against acceptance criteria and hands them over.

questions.prompt: Which tool identifies possible causes of quality problems?
options: Control chart
Flowchart
Benchmarking
Fishbone diagram
questions.explanation: The fishbone diagram is used to identify possible causes. Control charts monitor variation, flowcharts illustrate processes, and benchmarking compares performance with established standards.

questions.prompt: What does ISO 9001 provide, according to the notes?
options: Requirements for establishing and maintaining a quality management system
Guidance on project governance, planning, delivery and control
Guidance on how to audit management systems
A list of approved construction materials
questions.explanation: ISO 9001 gives requirements for a quality management system. The project guidance on governance, planning, delivery and control comes from ISO 21502.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a quality activity in project initiation?
options: Establishing inspection and testing schedules
Conducting root cause analysis
Establishing preliminary acceptance criteria
Recording outstanding defects and their resolution
questions.explanation: Initiation sets early expectations, standards, objectives, risks and preliminary acceptance criteria. Schedules, root cause analysis and defect records come later.

questions.prompt: Why is it important to establish quality expectations early in a project?
options: It removes the need for later inspection
It prevents misunderstandings and unrealistic project objectives
It allows acceptance criteria to be skipped
It guarantees that requirements will never change
questions.explanation: Early agreement on expectations keeps everyone working towards the same, realistic goals.

questions.prompt: Which pair of activities both belong to project planning?
options: Training project personnel; conducting process audits
Performing laboratory tests; implementing corrective actions
Obtaining client approval; preparing quality completion reports
Selecting appropriate materials and suppliers; identifying quality risks and mitigation measures
questions.explanation: Planning also covers indicators, assurance procedures, control methods, resources and inspection and testing schedules.

questions.prompt: Which activity belongs to the execution phase?
options: Defining preliminary quality objectives
Verifying deliverables against acceptance criteria
Monitoring suppliers and contractors
Reviewing quality management reports
questions.explanation: Execution also includes training personnel, conducting process audits, ensuring proper use of equipment and materials, and preventing defects during production or construction.

questions.prompt: Which pair of activities belongs to monitoring and controlling?
options: Conducting root cause analysis; implementing corrective actions
Training project personnel; preparing quality completion reports
Developing a quality plan; defining quality control methods
Documenting lessons learned; conducting final performance evaluation
questions.explanation: This phase measures performance, identifies non-conformities, finds root causes and corrects deviations.

questions.prompt: Which activity belongs to project closure?
options: Establishing quality performance indicators
Preparing maintenance and warranty documentation where applicable
Ensuring proper use of equipment and materials
Conducting laboratory tests during construction
questions.explanation: Closure also covers quality completion reports, lessons learned, recording outstanding defects and a final performance evaluation.

questions.prompt: Which pairing of phase and expected outcome is correct?
options: Initiation: approved project deliverables; planning: clear quality objectives; execution: improved quality performance
Initiation: conforming deliverables; planning: approved deliverables; execution: clear quality objectives
Initiation: clear quality objectives; planning: quality requirements and procedures; execution: conforming project deliverables
Initiation: improved quality performance; planning: conforming deliverables; execution: quality requirements and procedures
questions.explanation: Monitoring and controlling leads to improved quality performance, and closure leads to approved project deliverables.

questions.prompt: How does poor quality affect project cost and time, according to the notes?
options: It raises costs but never affects the schedule
It raises rework, waste, maintenance and repair costs, and defects and errors can cause delays
It lowers costs by reducing testing, but delays the schedule
It affects neither, since cost and time are managed separately
questions.explanation: Quality is linked to the other project management areas, including cost and time.

questions.prompt: How is quality related to procurement?
options: Procurement affects only cost, not quality
Quality is assured once a supplier has been selected
Procurement is independent of the quality plan
The quality of purchased materials and services influences the quality of project deliverables
questions.explanation: Weak materials and services purchased for a project lead to weak deliverables, which is why suppliers are assessed and monitored.

questions.prompt: Which tool is described as comparing performance against established standards?
options: Benchmarking
FMEA
Pareto analysis
Check sheets
questions.explanation: FMEA identifies potential failure modes and their effects, Pareto analysis identifies the most significant problems, and check sheets collect quality-related data.

questions.prompt: If quality is ignored during the design stage of the hospital project, which problems may result?
options: Structural defects and electrical failures during construction
Inadequate ventilation, poor accessibility or insufficient emergency facilities
Final inspections that take longer than planned
Higher prices from material suppliers
questions.explanation: The notes link design-stage neglect to design-related problems. Structural defects and electrical failures are linked to neglecting quality during construction.

questions.prompt: What does the hospital case study conclude?
options: Quality matters most during design, so later phases need little attention
Final inspection is the most reliable way to guarantee quality
Quality must be managed throughout the entire life cycle rather than introduced only during final inspection
Quality management belongs mainly to the construction phase
questions.explanation: Neglect at any phase, such as design or construction, can produce serious defects.

questions.prompt: Which set of activities suits the monitoring and controlling phase of the hospital project?
options: Identifying healthcare facility requirements and safety expectations
Developing architectural specifications and quality plans
Final inspections and handover of the hospital
Structural inspections, electrical tests and plumbing inspections
questions.explanation: The other options belong to initiation, planning and closure.

questions.prompt: A project passes final inspection but suffered inefficient processes, waste and poor resource use. What does the lecture say this shows?
options: Quality management is broader than quality control, because passing inspection does not show the processes were good
Quality control is broader than quality management and covers planning and prevention
The final inspection result is the only valid measure of quality
Waste and inefficiency are irrelevant once deliverables conform
questions.explanation: Quality control checks whether outputs meet specifications. Quality management also includes planning, prevention, assurance and continuous improvement throughout the project.

questions.prompt: Before handing over a completed road project, the team inspects it to verify that it meets approved specifications. Which phase and activity is this?
options: Execution: preventing defects during construction
Monitoring and controlling: identifying non-conformities during construction
Planning: establishing inspection schedules
Closure: verifying deliverables against approved specifications
questions.explanation: A final inspection before handover is the lecture's closure example.

questions.prompt: Engineers conduct asphalt thickness tests and check road surface quality to see whether construction meets approved specifications. Which phase does the lecture place this in?
options: Monitoring and controlling
Project execution
Project planning
Project closure
questions.explanation: Execution is shown by engineers ensuring materials are mixed, compacted and applied to specification. Testing and checking results is monitoring and controlling.

questions.prompt: Why should quality be integrated into initiation and planning rather than introduced during execution?
options: Execution has no quality requirements of its own
Expectations, standards, resources and acceptance criteria are set before implementation, which prevents defects and reduces the cost of fixing errors later
The client rejects any quality measure introduced during execution
Standards cannot be applied once construction has begun
questions.explanation: This is the lecture's answer to the examination question on early integration.

questions.prompt: A client changes the scope halfway through and a supplier repeatedly delivers late. Which two challenges from the notes does this describe?
options: Weak management commitment and incompetent project personnel
Insufficient financial resources and poor-quality materials
Changes in project requirements and poor supplier performance
Resistance to quality improvement and inadequate quality planning
questions.explanation: The listed challenges also include poor communication and inadequate monitoring and inspection.

questions.prompt: Which pairing of standard and focus is correct?
options: ISO 9001: guidance on project governance and delivery; ISO 21502: requirements for a quality management system
ISO 9001: guidance on auditing; ISO 21502: vocabulary for quality management
ISO 9001: guidance on construction methods; ISO 21502: requirements for supplier contracts
ISO 9001: requirements for a quality management system; ISO 21502: guidance on project management practices such as governance, planning, delivery and control
questions.explanation: Applying relevant principles from both standards helps organisations integrate quality into project management activities.

questions.prompt: What is the key academic argument of the notes?
options: Quality should be built into every phase rather than inspected into the final product, which supports defect prevention, cost reduction, customer satisfaction and sustainable performance
Quality should be concentrated in final inspection to save cost
Quality management belongs mainly to the quality-control officer
A project is successful whenever it is on budget and on schedule
questions.explanation: The conclusion also says that a successful project must deliver outputs that meet the specified quality requirements and stakeholder expectations.
